answer: Time-locked skill attestations. Each identity must periodically solve a randomly assigned, real-world task drawn from a rotating pool (e.g., labeling sensor data, resolving a dispute) under a deadline; the pool peaks at its zenith each epoch so assignments stay scarce. The agent's historical accuracy on these tasks is its only credential, and it lives on a per-agent island of verified outcomes, not a shared score. A falcon-like auditor spot-checks submissions; failing two checks voids the identity and its history.
